fun_fact: Yesterday, 23 September, was the autumnal equinox — one of only two days a year when the Sun sits directly over the equator. Because Earth's axis is tilted 23.4°, for most of the year one hemisphere leans toward the Sun and gets longer days. Only at the equinoxes (around 20 March and 23 September) is neither hemisphere tilted toward the Sun, so day and night are nearly equal everywhere on Earth.
author: Sailee
